sub_queries.hyde_text: We investigate the mechanism by which a student neural network inherits behavioral traits from a teacher network through model-generated training data that appears semantically neutral. We analyze teacher-student distillation setups where the teacher, fine-tuned to exhibit an entity preference, generates outputs conditioned on unrelated prompts; after filtering out overt instances of the trait via a judge model, the filtered outputs are used to fine-tune a student. Our analysis reveals that traits still transfer, indicating hidden statistical fingerprints in the teacher's generations. Using probing of the residual stream and parameter-level comparison of teacher and student LoRA updates, we localize where behavioral information is carried, and use causal patching to confirm that specific components propagate the trait. We further examine whether this phenomenon extends from language-model token supervised fine-tuning to denoising supervised fine-tuning in text-to-image diffusion transformers, where the training signal is per-timestep denoising over latent pixels rather than next-token prediction. Findings support the hypothesis that dark-knowledge transfer proceeds through non-obvious low-level features rather than the ostensible content of the training data, connecting to backdoor and data-poisoning phenomena in generative models, and depending critically on shared teacher-student initialization.
